card.name: Cham Dance
card.tagline: Bhutan's sacred masked Buddhist dance of merit and meditation
card.profile: The cham (Tibetan 'cham) is a masked and costumed dance of Tibetan Buddhism performed in Bhutan at Tshechu festivals, accompanied by monastic musicians on traditional instruments (Wikipedia). Dances depict incidents from the life of Padmasambhava and other saints and offer moral instruction relating to compassion; they are considered a form of meditation and an offering, performed by monks and laymen in elaborate masks and brocade robes to purify the ground and subdue evil. Tradition traces cham to the 8th century when Padmasambhava subdued local deities.
card.insight: Cham is a living sacred art rather than entertainment — a "meditation in action" in which dancers embody enlightened deities; in Bhutan its preservation is promoted by the Royal Academy of Performing Arts, and the related Drametse Ngacham (mask dance of the drums from Drametse) was proclaimed a Masterpiece in 2005 and inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List in 2008.
